mission_08: Standard cross-validation splits examples within a task, but meta-learning requires cross-validation across tasks to evaluate generalization to unseen tasks. Leave-one-task-out CV trains on all but one task and evaluates on the held-out task, providing an unbiased estimate of performance on new tasks. Task-stratified k-fold CV ensures each fold has a representative distribution of task types (e.g., easy vs. hard tasks, different domains). Nested cross-validation is essential for hyperparameter tuning in meta-learning: the inner loop selects hyperparameters using a subset of training tasks, while the outer loop evaluates the selected hyperparameters on held-out tasks, preventing overfitting to the validation set. Task augmentation — creating modified versions of tasks by subsampling, adding noise, or transforming features — can increase the effective number of tasks for more reliable CV estimates. Proper CV is critical in meta-learning because overfitting to the task distribution leads to poor generalization on truly novel tasks.
